author: ben_a_adams
content: The issue is charging a flat rate for very entirely different amounts of work; loading a 114 byte proxy costs the same gas as massive 64kB contract even though the time to load them from disk is very different

author: gaxanh
content:
What I mean is avoiding increasing the block gas limit so that we don’t have to keep increasing the cost of other bottlenecked resources. How many bytes of contract code a block can load is a separate question.

> The issue is charging a flat rate for very entirely different amounts of work; loading a 114 byte proxy costs the same gas as massive 64kB contract even though the time to load them from disk is very different
Is the cost of loading contract code supposed to scale linearly or in steps? EIP-2929 suggests that loading 24 kB of data is effectively no different from loading just 32 bytes. If that is the intended model, then a stepwise pricing scheme would seem more appropriate.

author: ben_a_adams
content: The 24kB as flat is so is same as today (currently can only deploy 24kB contracts); in Glamsterdam that limit goes to 64kB which causes the issue we are seeing

author: gaxanh
content:
So, with the current block limits in Glamsterdam, can we already accommodate 64 kB contracts?

If the answer is yes, and the goal is to increase throughput in subsequent hard forks, then the only way to do that without increasing the block limit is to reduce the cost of the resources we specifically want to scale.

That’s all I mean.

author: ben_a_adams
content: And why isn't the number of contracts that can be run per block one of the things we want to scale?

author: ben_a_adams
content: Also contract loading takes away from disk resources for SLOAD and STORE directly also
